prompt: In the $S_z$ basis, $S_x = \frac{\hbar}{2}\big(|+\rangle\langle-| + |-\rangle\langle+|\big)$. Show that $|S_x;\pm\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\big(|+\rangle \pm |-\rangle\big)$ are eigenstates of $S_x$, and give their eigenvalues.
solution:
Note $S_x|+\rangle = \frac{\hbar}{2}|-\rangle$ and $S_x|-\rangle = \frac{\hbar}{2}|+\rangle$. Then

$$S_x\,|S_x;\pm\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,\frac{\hbar}{2}\big(|-\rangle \pm |+\rangle\big) = \pm\frac{\hbar}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\big(|+\rangle \pm |-\rangle\big) = \pm\frac{\hbar}{2}\,|S_x;\pm\rangle.$$

So the eigenvalues are $\pm\hbar/2$ — the two outcomes of an $S_x$ measurement.

prompt: Using $S_i = \frac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_i$ and the Pauli matrices, verify the commutation relation $[S_x, S_y] = i\hbar\,S_z$.
solution:
Since $[S_x, S_y] = \frac{\hbar^2}{4}[\sigma_x, \sigma_y]$, compute the products:

$$\sigma_x\sigma_y = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -i \\ i & 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} i & 0 \\ 0 & -i \end{pmatrix} = i\sigma_z, \qquad \sigma_y\sigma_x = -i\sigma_z.$$

Hence $[\sigma_x, \sigma_y] = 2i\sigma_z$, and

$$[S_x, S_y] = \frac{\hbar^2}{4}\,(2i\sigma_z) = i\hbar\,\frac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_z = i\hbar\,S_z.$$

prompt: An $S_z = +\hbar/2$ beam is sent through an $\hat{x}$-oriented SG apparatus; its $S_x = +\hbar/2$ output is then sent through a $\hat{z}$-oriented apparatus. What fraction of the atoms leaving the second apparatus emerge with $S_z = -\hbar/2$?
solution:
The state entering the third apparatus is $|S_x;+\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\big(|+\rangle + |-\rangle\big)$, so

$$P(S_z = -\tfrac{\hbar}{2}) = |\langle - | S_x;+\rangle|^2 = \left|\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right|^2 = \frac{1}{2}.$$

Half. The original $S_z = +\hbar/2$ preparation is irrelevant — the intervening $S_x$ measurement erased it, which is precisely the sense in which $S_x$ and $S_z$ are incompatible.
